title: Five-Item Sprint Almanac — Elya Dimitrov
content:
Quick note: this is the 5-item sprint almanac I actually use when I feel scattered. Keep it under 10 minutes every morning or at the top of the work block.

Purpose:
- Create a tiny, high-confidence day plan that maps to measurable outcomes.
- Force prioritization (exactly 5 things).
- Track small signal metrics for momentum: throughput, focus, blockers.

Ritual (5–10 minutes):
1) Write date and three-word intention.
2) List 5 items: 3 outcome-focused, 1 maintenance, 1 experiment/learning.
3) For each item: add expected time (min), success criterion (quick), and a single metric if applicable.
4) Commit: checkboxes and a single highlighted top-1.
5) End-of-day micro-retro: fill mini-retro (W / WN / Next experiment).

Template (copy into daily note):
- Date: 2025-07-02 — Intention: "Ship a small win"
- Top-1 (shrink the scope): Finish review + merge for analytics-schema PR — 45m — success = merged; metric = PR merged by EOD
- Item 2: Draft notes for customer sync (outcome: clear ask) — 30m — success = 3 action items created
- Item 3: Quick refactor in personal utils (maintenance) — 25m — success = tests pass; metric = CI green
- Item 4: Experiment: try Pomodoro-ish 25/5 for the review task — 50m total — success = subjectively better focus score
- Item 5: Tidy inbox & triage (maintenance) — 15m — success = inbox < 10 unread

Signal metrics I track (tiny):
- Throughput: completed items / 5
- Focus score: 1–10 (self-rated after main block)
- Blocker minutes: total minutes stuck waiting on others or unclear specs
- Quality shard: number of follow-ups generated by completed items (lower is better)

Example micro-retro (to copy/paste at EOD):
- Wins: merged analytics-schema PR; got clear ask from customer; inbox trimmed
- What went not: drifted into debugging session for 90m (scope creep) — lost time
- What next (experiment): enforce a hard 45m cap on review; if still blocking, switch to pairing or leave comment and move on
- Signal numbers: throughput 3/5; focus 6/10; blocker minutes 30; follow-ups 1

Hypotheses to test (kept light):
- H1: capping the review task to 45m + a pairing fallback will reduce blocker minutes by 40% week-over-week.
- H2: 25/5 Pomodoro for review tasks yields recognition of fewer context switches and higher focus score on average (target +1 point).

Notes to self / shorthand (informal):
- If top-1 is infra/CI related, move it earlier in day.
- Small wins compound — aim for at least 1 meaningful deliverable per day even if other items are incomplete.
- Keep an eye on follow-ups metric: if >2 per day, reassess definition of "done".

Open questions / friction points:
- How to account for deep-focus days vs meeting-heavy days? (maybe allow a 2-item variant with higher expected time)
- Should weekly roll-ups be automated? (temptation to make a sheet)
- When experiments repeat without improvement, stop them after 3 iterations.

Quick log (recent entries):
- 2025-06-30: throughput 4/5, focus 7, blocker 10m — shipped small feature toggle (good)
- 2025-07-01: throughput 2/5, focus 5, blocker 45m — meetings killed deep work
- 2025-07-02 (today): planned; will update EOD

Next actions (one-liners):
- Try enforced 45m cap on review tomorrow morning (block calendar)
- Create a lightweight weekly sheet (2 columns) for throughput and average focus to spot trends
- If Pomodoro helps 2x in a week, adopt as default for review-heavy days

References / quick links:
- confluence://personal/mini-sprints (my longer write-up)
- slack://pm-sync/thread (notes from customer sync)
- JIRA-PLANS-123 (planning backlog for small experiments)

Random thought (notes-to-self):
- The almanac framing helps because it's low ceremony. When I make it fancy (sheets, dashboards) it becomes another project. Keep it handheld and fast.

End of note.

-- Elya
